lead: A synchronous machine keeps its rotor at one speed fixed by the supply frequency. The rotor carries a DC field; the stator carries a three-phase armature. The two fields lock together, so speed does not fall as load rises. That gives steady frequency for generation and exact speed for drives. The same machine works as a generator in power stations and as a motor for constant-speed loads or power-factor correction. It cannot start as a motor without help.
prereq: You need: Chapter 3.2 for the induced-EMF form, Chapter 3.5 for synchronous speed, and Unit 2 for star connections.

sections.h3: One speed, set by the supply

blocks.text: Construction puts the field on the rotor and the three-phase armature on the stator. The rotor field is fed with direct current (DC) through slip rings, or is made with permanent magnets. Stator currents produce a rotating magnetic field. The rotor poles lock to that field, so the rotor turns at the field speed. This is synchronous speed.

blocks.where: N<sub>s</sub> is synchronous speed in rpm; f is supply frequency in Hz; P is number of poles.

blocks.text: Pole shape follows speed. A cylindrical rotor is long and thin for high-speed turbines. A salient-pole rotor has projecting poles for low-speed hydro sets. For a generator, the prime mover turns the rotor, and the frequency is set by speed and poles.

blocks.where: f is generated frequency in Hz; P is number of poles; N is rotor speed in rpm.

blocks.text: A motor needs help to start. At standstill the alternating torque averages zero, so the rotor cannot pull into step by itself. A damper winding, which is a shorted cage on the rotor, lets it start like an induction motor. A small helper motor, called a pony motor, or a variable-frequency drive can also bring it near synchronous speed.

Field current sets power factor. With constant load, armature current is least at unity power factor, where current is in phase with voltage. It rises when field current is too low (lagging) or too high (leading). A plot of armature current against field current is the V-curve. Its dip is the unity-power-factor point. Here pu means per unit, a multiple of a chosen base value.
Each phase of the armature has T turns in series. The rotating flux per pole Φ induces an RMS phase EMF. The equation assumes a sinusoidal flux wave.

blocks.where: E<sub>ph</sub> is RMS phase EMF in volts; f is frequency in Hz; Φ is flux per pole in weber; T is turns per phase in series.

blocks.text: Use E<sub>ph</sub> with phase voltage, never line voltage. At no load, in a star connection the line EMF is √3 times the phase EMF, and line current equals phase current. In a delta connection line EMF equals phase EMF.

blocks.where: V<sub>L</sub> is open-circuit line EMF in volts; E<sub>ph</sub> is generated phase EMF in volts. This holds for a star-connected armature at no load. Under load, armature reaction and synchronous impedance reduce terminal voltage; use V<sub>ph</sub> = E<sub>ph</sub> − I<sub>a</sub> Z<sub>s</sub> in phasor form, where V<sub>ph</sub> is terminal phase voltage, I<sub>a</sub> is armature current and Z<sub>s</sub> is synchronous impedance.

blocks.text: The worked example below combines the speed-frequency relation, the EMF equation and the star open-circuit line-voltage relation.

sections.h3: Starting, control and where they are used

blocks.text: On start, the damper winding produces induction-motor torque and brings the rotor close to synchronous speed. The DC field is then switched on, and the rotor pulls into synchronism. Once locked, steady speed stays N<sub>s</sub>; extra load changes the torque angle, not the speed.

An overexcited synchronous motor draws a leading current. At no load it acts as a synchronous condenser, supplying reactive power and correcting power factor. An underexcited motor draws a lagging current. Field current is varied continuously by a field rheostat or automatic exciter/AVR (automatic voltage regulator) to set the power factor.

Large alternators in thermal, hydro and nuclear stations are synchronous generators. Synchronous condensers sit at substations for voltage and power-factor support. Constant-speed drives such as large compressors and mills use synchronous motors. Permanent-magnet synchronous machines, covered with special machines in Chapter 3.8, are common in efficient variable-speed drives.

figure.caption: Armature current is lowest at 4 pu field current, the unity-power-factor point, and rises on both sides as the motor becomes lagging or leading.

spec.aria: The V-curve: armature current falls to a minimum of 1 per unit at 4 per unit field current, where the motor runs at unity power factor, and rises on either side.

examples.question: A three-phase, star-connected alternator has 4 poles and runs at 1500 rpm. Each phase has 200 turns in series and the flux per pole is 0.02 Wb. Find the frequency, the EMF per phase and the line voltage.
steps: Number of poles P = 4; speed N = 1500 rpm.
Flux per pole Φ = 0.02 Wb; turns per phase T = 200.
Phase EMF E<sub>ph</sub> = 4.44 f Φ T = 4.44 × 50 × 0.02 × 200.
Star open-circuit line EMF V<sub>L</sub> = √3 × E<sub>ph</sub> = 1.732 × 888 V = 1538 V to the nearest volt.
examples.answer: Frequency = 50 Hz, phase EMF = 888 V, open-circuit line EMF = 1538 V.
examples.check:
f = 4*1500/120
Phi = 0.02
T = 200
Eph = 4.44*f*Phi*T
Vline = (3**0.5)*Eph
print(round(f, 2))
print(round(Eph, 2))
print(round(Vline, 0))

traps: A synchronous motor cannot start from rest on a fixed-frequency supply; it needs a damper winding, pony motor or variable-frequency source.
Do not put line voltage into E<sub>ph</sub> = 4.44 f Φ T; that equation gives phase EMF. Convert with √3 for a star connection.
Use rpm in f = P N / 120. Using revolutions per second without the 60 factor gives a frequency 60 times too small.
Field current in a synchronous motor changes power factor and armature current, not steady speed; speed stays N<sub>s</sub>.
Do not confuse synchronous speed with actual rotor speed in an induction motor; a synchronous machine has no slip in steady state.

quiz.q: Write the relation between frequency, poles and speed for a synchronous generator.
quiz.a: f = P N / 120, where f is frequency in Hz, P is number of poles and N is speed in rpm.

quiz.q: Why can a synchronous motor not start by itself from a fixed-frequency supply?
quiz.a: At standstill the stator field sweeps past the rotor poles, so the torque reverses every half cycle and averages zero. The rotor cannot accelerate and lock. A damper winding, pony motor or variable-frequency drive brings it near synchronous speed first.

quiz.q: A 6-pole synchronous generator runs at 1000 rpm. Find its frequency.
A star-connected alternator has a phase EMF of 400 V at no load. Find the open-circuit line voltage.
quiz.a: V<sub>L</sub> = √3 × 400 V = 693 V to the nearest volt. This is the no-load line EMF; under load the terminal line voltage differs because of armature reaction and synchronous impedance.

quiz.q: Why does the armature current of a synchronous motor show a minimum in the V-curve?
quiz.a: At the minimum, field current is just enough to give unity power factor. The motor draws only active current. Too little field current makes the current lag; too much makes it lead. Both add a reactive component, so the armature current rises on either side of the dip.

quiz.q: A synchronous motor is overexcited at constant load. State the effect on armature current and power factor.
quiz.a: The motor draws a leading current. Power factor becomes leading, and armature current rises above its unity-power-factor value because the reactive component increases.

quiz.q: Why is a salient-pole rotor used in a low-speed hydro generator?
quiz.a: Many projecting poles give the large pole number needed for 50 Hz at low speed. They also give a sturdy mechanical shape for a large slow rotor.

beyond: Not for the exam. Grid operators now use synchronous condensers to add inertia and short-circuit strength as coal plants retire. Wind and solar farms with power-electronic converters need such support for stable voltage. Permanent-magnet synchronous machines dominate efficient electric vehicles and ship drives. Search next for synchronous condenser, grid inertia, damper winding and PMSM field-oriented control.
